subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Toy Party
hook: Watch how Arjun and Mitthu bring toys together and discover addition!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A curious 6-year-old learning to add toys

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A clever parrot who loves combining things

slides.title: Arjun and Mitthu's Toy Party
slides.inSimpleWords: Let's learn addition with toys and a clever parrot!

slides.title: Time for a Toy Party!
slides.storyContext: Arjun sits on the floor with a pile of toys. Mitthu lands beside him. 'Let's make a big pile!' says Arjun. 'When we put toys together, we add!' chirps Mitthu wisely.
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun and Mitthu put toys together to play.

image.alt: Time for a Toy Party! — Addition

slides.title: What is Addition?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Addition means taking two groups and putting them together to make one bigger group. Watch!'

points.label: We use the + sign
points.text: It shows we are joining things

slides.inSimpleWords: Addition is when we put things together.

slides.title: Two Toy Cars
slides.storyContext: Arjun places one red toy car on the floor. Then he picks up one blue toy car. 'Look, Mitthu! One car... and one more car!' Mitthu hops up and down. 'That's two cars now!'

points.text: One car plus one car makes two

slides.title: Counting Both Groups
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows Arjun how to count. 'First group has 1. Second group has 1. Together: count them all! One, two. That's 2 total!'

points.label: How to add
points.text: Count all the objects after combining

example.problem: You have 1 toy. A friend gives you 1 more. How many now?

slides.inSimpleWords: Count everything together to find the answer.

slides.title: Adding on Fingers
slides.storyContext: Arjun holds up one finger on his left hand. 'One car here.' Then one finger on his right hand. 'One car here.' He brings them together. 'One plus one makes two!' Mitthu claps.

points.label: Fast way to add
points.text: Use fingers instead of counting objects

slides.inSimpleWords: Use your fingers to add numbers.

slides.title: Two Balls and One More
slides.storyContext: Arjun rolls out two red balls. 'Two balls,' he counts. Then he rolls one yellow ball next to them. 'And... one more!' Mitthu flies over. 'That's three balls total! Two plus one is three!'

image.alt: Two Balls and One More — Addition

slides.title: Adding 2 + 1 with Fingers
slides.storyContext: Arjun holds up two fingers. 'Two balls here.' Then adds one more finger. 'One more ball!' He counts all three fingers. 'Two plus one makes three!'

points.text: Hold two fingers, add one more

slides.title: The Plus Sign
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points at a drawing. 'Look! The plus sign + means we are joining! It has a line going across and a line going down. It means ADD!

points.label: The + symbol
points.text: Means we put two groups together

points.label: It looks like
points.text: A cross with horizontal and vertical lines

slides.inSimpleWords: The plus sign tells us to add.

slides.title: Blocks Stack Taller
slides.storyContext: Arjun stacks three blue blocks. Then he stacks two more blocks on top. 'Three blocks... then two more blocks!' He counts them all. Mitthu looks amazed. 'Five blocks now! Three plus two is five!'

slides.title: Practice: 3 + 2
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges: 'Arjun, hold up three fingers on one hand. Now add two more on your other hand. Count them all!' Arjun carefully counts. 'One, two, three... four, five! That's five!'

points.label: Try it
points.text: Hold up fingers and count the total

example.solution: Hold 3 fingers, add 2 more, count all: 5

slides.title: The Teddy and Dolls
slides.storyContext: Arjun lines up one teddy bear. Next to it, he arranges three dolls. 'One teddy... three dolls... let's add!' One teddy plus three dolls makes four friends! Mitthu nods. 'One plus three is four!'

slides.title: Different Groups, Same Answer
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows: 'One plus three makes four. But also, two plus two makes four! And three plus one makes four too! Same answer, different ways!'
slides.inSimpleWords: You can make the same number in different ways.

slides.title: Make Your Own Addition
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges Arjun: 'Pick any two groups of toys and add them together! Count what you get!' Arjun picks two toy trains and three toy elephants. 'Two plus three... that's five!'

points.label: Try adding
points.text: Pick toys and add them to find the answer

slides.inSimpleWords: You can add any two groups together.

slides.title: Adding by Counting On
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches a fast trick: 'If you have 2 toys already, don't count from one! Start at 2, then count up: 2... three, four, five! You added 3 to 2 and got 5!'

points.label: Counting on
points.text: Start with the bigger number and count up

points.label: It's faster
points.text: Don't count from one every time

slides.inSimpleWords: Count on from the bigger number.

slides.title: Toy Party Gets Bigger!
slides.storyContext: Mitthu suggests, 'Let's add bigger numbers now!' Arjun arranges four building blocks and four toy cars. 'Four plus four...' He counts the whole pile slowly. '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8! That's eight!'

slides.title: Big Addition: 4 + 4 = 8
slides.storyContext: Arjun uses his fingers: 'Four fingers on this hand, four on that hand. Together...' He counts carefully: '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Mitthu, that's eight!'

points.text: Doubles are when both sides are the same

slides.title: Doubles — The Same Number Twice
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'When you add a number to itself, it's called a double! One plus one is a double. Two plus two is a double. Three plus three is a double!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Doubles are when you add a number to itself.

slides.title: Find All the Doubles
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges: 'Show me 1+1, 2+2, 3+3 using your fingers or toys!' Arjun carefully creates each one and counts. 'Two, four, six!' Mitthu chirps, 'Perfect! All doubles!'

slides.title: More Than Eight
slides.storyContext: Arjun keeps adding! Five blocks plus three blocks. 'One, two, three, four, five... six, seven, eight! That's eight!' Mitthu nods. 'You're getting good at this, Arjun!'

slides.title: Practice: 5 + 3 = 8
slides.storyContext: Arjun shows: 'Five fingers on one hand, three on the other. Count the total: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... 6, 7, 8. That's eight!'

slides.title: Real-Life Adding
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'If you have 2 apples and your friend gives you 4 more, how many do you have?' Arjun thinks hard. 'Two apples... plus four more... that's six!'

points.label: Adding in real life
points.text: You can use addition for anything!

slides.inSimpleWords: You can add anything — toys, fruits, animals!

slides.title: The Equals Sign
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points: 'Look! The equals sign = means both sides are the same. Two plus three equals five. That means 2+3 and 5 are the same!'

points.label: The = symbol
points.text: Means the answer is what comes after

slides.inSimpleWords: The equals sign shows the answer.

slides.title: Group Games
slides.storyContext: Mitthu organizes a game. 'Arjun, gather your friends! Three friends here, two friends there.' They count: 'Three plus two makes five! Five friends to play with!'

slides.title: Finding More Doubles
slides.storyContext: Mitthu continues: 'What about 5 + 5? Or 6 + 6? Can you count them?' Arjun carefully counts each double. 'Five plus five is ten! Six plus six is twelve!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Bigger numbers can be doubles too.

slides.title: Adding Order Doesn't Matter
slides.storyContext: Mitthu shows: 'Two plus three is five. Three plus two is also five! The order doesn't matter when we add!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Addition works the same way either way.

slides.title: We Can Add!
slides.storyContext: All the toys are in one big happy pile. Mitthu sings: 'When we put toys together, we add! One plus one, two plus one, three plus two... addition is putting things with things!' Arjun giggles.

points.label: You can add with
points.text: Fingers, toys, or anything you count

slides.inSimpleWords: Addition is putting groups together to count.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu's Treat Sharing
hook: Discover subtraction when Arjun and Mitthu share treats!

characters.name: Arjun
characters.role: A 6-year-old learning to take away and share

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A thoughtful parrot helping with sharing

slides.title: Arjun and Mitthu's Treat Sharing
slides.inSimpleWords: Let's learn subtraction by sharing treats!

slides.title: Treats in the Bowl
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom gives him a bowl with five yummy biscuits. Mitthu smells them and says, 'Wow! We need to share these!' Arjun nods happily. 'Let's take some away and count what's left!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun has treats to share with Mitthu.

slides.title: What is Subtraction?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Subtraction means taking away! We start with some, we take some away, and we find what's left. Like this...'

points.label: We use the - sign
points.text: It shows we are removing things

slides.inSimpleWords: Subtraction is when we take things away.

slides.title: One Biscuit Away
slides.storyContext: Arjun counts five biscuits in the bowl. 'Five!' Then he takes one biscuit out for Mitthu. 'I'm taking one away.' He counts what's left: 'One, two, three, four. That's four biscuits now!'

points.text: When we take one away from five, four is left

slides.title: Showing 5 - 1 on Fingers
slides.storyContext: Arjun holds up five fingers. 'Five biscuits.' Then puts one finger down. 'One away.' He counts what's up: 'One, two, three, four. That's four left!'

slides.title: Counting Down
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'When we take away, we count backwards!' Arjun had four biscuits. He gives one to his little sister. 'Four, three... three left!' Mitthu nods wisely. 'We count down from four to three!'
slides.inSimpleWords: When we take away, we count backwards.

slides.title: Three Biscuits, One Crumb
slides.storyContext: Arjun has three biscuits on his plate. 'Crunch! Crunch!' He eats one. Mitthu watches and counts: 'You had three. You ate one. Now you have... one, two. That's two left!'

points.text: Three take away one is two

slides.title: Taking Away More
slides.storyContext: Arjun shows Mitthu six fruits: four apples and two oranges. 'Let's take away two apples!' He moves them aside. Mitthu counts: 'One, two, three, four fruits stay. Six take away two is four!'

points.text: Six take away two is four

slides.title: The Minus Sign
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points at a drawing. 'Look! The minus sign - means we are taking away. It has just one line going across. It means SUBTRACT!'

points.label: The - symbol
points.text: Means we are removing or taking away

slides.inSimpleWords: The minus sign tells us to subtract.

slides.title: Practice: 6 - 2 = 4
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges: 'Hold up six fingers. Now put two down. Count what's still up!' Arjun counts: 'One, two, three, four. That's four!'

slides.title: Share with Friends
slides.storyContext: Arjun has five toy cars. His friend Ravi comes to play. 'Let's give Ravi two cars!' says Arjun. He counts what he has left: 'One, two, three. Three cars still mine. Five take away two is three!'

points.text: Five take away two is three

slides.title: Showing 5 - 2 with Objects
slides.storyContext: Arjun arranges five toy cars in a line. 'Five cars.' He moves two cars away. 'Two away.' He counts what's left. 'One, two, three. That's three!'

slides.title: Subtraction Facts to Remember
slides.storyContext: Mitthu creates a chart: 'Here are important subtraction facts! Five minus one is four. Four minus one is three. Three minus one is two!'

slides.title: Mitthu's Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sets up a challenge: 'I have seven seeds. I eat three. How many are left?' Arjun counts carefully on his fingers. '7... take away 3... is 4!' Mitthu chirps happily.

slides.title: Counting Back to Subtract
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'Here's a trick! To subtract three from seven, start at seven and count backwards three times: 7... 6, 5, 4. That's your answer!'

points.label: Count back method
points.text: Start at the big number, count down by the small number

points.label: Fast way to subtract
points.text: Don't count from one each time

slides.title: Empty Bowl
slides.storyContext: Arjun's mom makes more treats! Now there are eight samosas in a plate. Arjun and Mitthu eat them all one by one. 'Eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one...' Finally: 'Zero! All gone!'

points.label: Subtracting all
points.text: If we take away everything, nothing is left

slides.title: Subtracting All: 8 - 8 = 0
slides.storyContext: Arjun has eight samosas. He gives away eight. 'Eight take away eight...' He counts what's left. 'Nothing! Zero samosas left!'

points.text: Any number minus itself equals zero

slides.inSimpleWords: When you take away all, zero is left.

slides.title: Real-Life Subtraction
slides.storyContext: Mitthu asks: 'If you have 7 candies and eat 2, how many are left?' Arjun thinks. 'Seven candies... take away two... that's five!'

points.label: Subtracting in real life
points.text: You use subtraction when you give things away or use things up

slides.inSimpleWords: You subtract when things go away.

slides.title: Addition and Subtraction Are Opposite
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Watch! If 2 + 3 = 5, then 5 - 3 = 2. They work backwards! Addition puts things together. Subtraction takes them apart!'

slides.title: More Treats to Share
slides.storyContext: Mitthu suggests more challenges: 'Arjun, if I have six biscuits and eat one, how many are left?' Arjun counts: 'Six take away one is five! That's five biscuits left!'

points.text: Six take away one is five

slides.title: Even More Subtraction
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges: 'If we have eight toys and remove four, how many stay?' Arjun uses his fingers carefully. 'Eight take away four is four! Four toys left!'

points.text: Eight take away four is four

slides.title: Subtraction Fact Families
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Look! Five minus two is three. And two plus three is five. They go together! That's a fact family!'

slides.title: Bigger Subtraction
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges with bigger numbers: 'Arjun, if we have nine biscuits and share four, how many stay?' Arjun counts backward: 'Nine, eight, seven, six, five! Five biscuits left!'

points.text: Nine take away four is five

slides.title: Practice: 9 - 4 = 5
slides.storyContext: Arjun practices with fingers and counting. 'Nine take away four... count back: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5. That's five left!' Mitthu chirps, 'Perfect! You're a subtraction expert!'

slides.title: Checking Subtraction with Addition
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches a trick: 'If six take away two is four, then four plus two should make six! Let's check: 4 + 2 = 6! Yes, our subtraction was right!'

slides.title: Taking Away
slides.storyContext: Mitthu sits on Arjun's shoulder. 'Subtraction means taking away! Five take away two is three. Three take away one is two. We count down and find what's left!'

points.label: Subtraction is
points.text: Taking away and counting what stays

points.label: You can subtract
points.text: Toys, fruits, or anything you count

slides.inSimpleWords: Subtraction is taking away to find what's left.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arjun and Mitthu Find Shapes Everywhere
hook: Search the neighborhood with Arjun and Mitthu to find circles, squares, and triangles!

characters.name: Mitthu
characters.role: A shape-loving parrot who points out patterns

slides.title: Arjun and Mitthu Find Shapes Everywhere
slides.inSimpleWords: Let's discover circles, squares, triangles, and more!

slides.title: A Shape Hunt Begins!
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Mitthu look out the window. Mitthu cries out, 'Arjun! Look! Shapes everywhere!' Arjun's eyes grow wide. 'Let's find them all!' Off they go on a shape adventure through their neighborhood.
slides.inSimpleWords: Arjun and Mitthu go hunting for shapes.

image.alt: A Shape Hunt Begins! — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: What Are Shapes?
slides.storyContext: Mitthu explains: 'Shapes are the outlines of things! Everything around us has a shape. Some are round, some have corners, some have points!'

points.label: A shape is
points.text: The outline or form of something

slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes are the forms of things around us.

slides.title: Circle, Circle!
slides.storyContext: They walk to the park. Mitthu points at the big round clock on the tower. 'That's a circle, Arjun! Round all the way around!' Then they spot a ball rolling by. 'Another circle!' Arjun laughs.

points.label: Circle
points.text: Round like a ball or a plate

slides.inSimpleWords: Circles are round like a ball.

slides.title: Finding Circles
slides.storyContext: Arjun points around: 'A clock is a circle! A plate is a circle! A wheel is a circle!' Mitthu adds, 'See how they're all round? No corners, just smooth and curved!'

points.label: Circles have
points.text: No corners, just one curved line

points.label: Round all over
points.text: The same distance from center to edge

example.solution: Circles — like clocks, plates, balls, wheels

slides.title: Square Windows
slides.storyContext: At the shopkeeper's house, Arjun points up. 'Look! Four sides, all the same!' Mitthu agrees, 'That's a square, Arjun. See? The window is a square. Four corners, four sides that are all the same size!'

points.label: All sides the same
points.text: It looks like a perfect box

example.solution: A square has four equal sides

slides.title: Triangle Pizza!
slides.storyContext: Arjun's stomach rumbles. They peek into the pizza shop. 'Look, Mitthu! Triangles!' The pizza slices are triangles with three sides and three corners. Mitthu hops: 'Three! That's why it's called a triangle!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Triangles have three sides and three corners.

slides.title: Finding Triangles
slides.storyContext: Arjun spots more triangles: 'A roof is a triangle! A slice of pie is a triangle! A tent is a triangle!' Mitthu nods wisely. 'Three sides, three corners, every time!'

points.label: Triangles have
points.text: Three straight sides and three corners

example.solution: Triangles — like roofs, pizza slices, tents

slides.title: Rectangle Doors
slides.storyContext: They pass a shop with a tall door. 'That's not a square!' says Arjun. Mitthu nods wisely. 'It's a rectangle! It has four sides, but two are longer. Long and short sides, four corners!'

points.label: Rectangle
points.text: Four sides, but two long and two short

points.label: Different from square
points.text: Not all sides are the same length

example.problem: Is this door a square or rectangle?
example.solution: Rectangle — it's taller than it is wide

slides.inSimpleWords: Rectangles are longer on two sides.

slides.title: Find Rectangles!
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges: 'Find things that are rectangular! Not as wide as they are tall!' Arjun looks around. 'A book! A door! A flag!' Mitthu chirps, 'All rectangles!'

points.label: Rectangles are
points.text: Wider or taller, but not equal

example.solution: Yes! It's taller than it is wide

slides.title: Star in the Sky
slides.storyContext: It's getting evening. Mitthu points up at a drawn star on a poster. 'A star! It has pointy corners!' Arjun counts: 'One, two, three, four, five... five pointy corners! That's a star!'

image.alt: Star in the Sky — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: Finding Stars
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to the sky. 'Real stars! And see on the flag? That's a star! And on the badge!' Mitthu adds, 'Five points, every time. One, two, three, four, five!'

example.problem: How many points on a star?

slides.title: Counting Sides and Corners
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches: 'Every shape has sides and corners. Sides are the lines. Corners are where sides meet. Count them to know the shape!'

points.label: Sides are
points.text: The lines that make up a shape

slides.inSimpleWords: Count sides and corners to find shapes.

slides.title: Mitthu's Shape Game
slides.storyContext: Mitthu creates a challenge: 'I'll describe a shape. You guess it! Round and flat, no corners at all.' Arjun jumps up. 'A circle!' Mitthu continues: 'Four equal sides and four corners!' Arjun shouts, 'A square!'

points.label: Guess the shape
points.text: Listen to clues about sides and corners

slides.inSimpleWords: You can guess shapes by counting sides.

image.alt: Mitthu's Shape Game — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: Shapes All Around
slides.storyContext: Arjun looks around and spots more shapes: 'The biscuit tin is a square! The car wheel is a circle! The tent is a triangle!' Mitthu claps his wings. 'Shapes are everywhere, Arjun! Everywhere!'
slides.inSimpleWords: We see shapes in everything around us.

image.alt: Shapes All Around — Shapes Around Us

slides.title: Drawing Shapes
slides.storyContext: Mitthu suggests: 'Let's draw shapes! A circle — just curve around. A square — four sides. A triangle — three sides. See? Anyone can draw them!'

points.label: You can draw
points.text: Any shape with a pencil or pen

slides.title: Shape Hunt Challenge
slides.storyContext: Mitthu says: 'Now you hunt! Find a circle, a square, a triangle, a rectangle, and a star in your house. Come back and show me!' Arjun nods eagerly and runs off.

points.label: Hunt for shapes
points.text: Find each shape in your surroundings

slides.inSimpleWords: Hunt for shapes in your home!

slides.title: 3D Shapes Too
slides.storyContext: Mitthu points: 'Wait! We also have cube shapes! A dice is a cube — it's like a square but thicker! A ball is like a circle but round all the way around!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Some shapes are thick and round!

slides.title: Exploring 3D Shapes
slides.storyContext: Arjun picks up a dice and a ball. 'This dice is like a square but it's thick! And this ball is like a circle that goes all around!' Mitthu nods. 'They have height, width, AND depth!'

example.problem: Is a dice a square or a cube?

slides.title: More Shape Exploration
slides.storyContext: Mitthu keeps finding shapes! 'Look at the fence! It's made of rectangles. The sign is a rectangle too!' Arjun nods excitedly. 'Rectangles are everywhere! Long shapes!'

points.label: Rectangles are
points.text: Longer than they are tall (or vice versa)

slides.title: Sorting Shapes
slides.storyContext: Mitthu creates groups: 'Here are circles: clock, wheel, plate. Squares: box, tile, coaster. Triangles: roof, pizza, flag. Can you sort more shapes?'

points.label: Practice
points.text: Find and group shapes by type

example.problem: Is a coin a circle or a square?
example.solution: A circle! Round with no corners

slides.title: Shapes in Buildings
slides.storyContext: They look at a house. 'The walls are rectangles. The roof is a triangle. The door is a rectangle. The window is a square!' Mitthu chirps, 'Buildings are made from shapes!'

slides.title: Create with Shapes
slides.storyContext: Mitthu challenges: 'Can you make a picture using shapes? Use circles for eyes, a triangle for a nose, and a rectangle for a mouth!' Arjun draws happily, creating a face from shapes.

example.solution: Circles for eyes, triangle for nose, line for mouth

slides.inSimpleWords: You can make pictures with shapes!

slides.title: Shapes in Your Bedroom
slides.storyContext: Mitthu looks around Arjun's room. 'Your bed is a rectangle! Your pillow is a rectangle! Even your rug is a square! Everything is shapes!' Arjun laughs. 'Even my toy box is a cube!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Your room is full of shapes.

slides.title: Recognizing Shapes Anywhere
slides.storyContext: Mitthu teaches the final lesson: 'Now you know how to find shapes everywhere! Look for sides, corners, and curves. Every shape tells a story!'

points.label: Shape skills
points.text: You can identify shapes anywhere now!

points.label: Remember
points.text: Count sides and corners to identify shapes

slides.inSimpleWords: You are a shape expert now!

slides.title: All the Shapes
slides.storyContext: Back home, Mitthu summarizes on Arjun's shoulder: 'Circle is round. Square has four equal sides. Rectangle has four sides but two are longer. Triangle has three sides. Star has five points! Remember them?'
slides.inSimpleWords: Shapes are circles, squares, rectangles, triangles, and stars.

image.alt: All the Shapes — Shapes Around Us
